# Results — Study 464 (Pennant)

*Generated by [`examples/verify.py`](../examples/verify.py). The believers' claim — **a pennant
continues the prior thrust: after a steep pole and a tight converging pause, price breaks out in
the pole's direction and runs further** — encoded as a mechanical rule. A pole is a cumulative
move over 8 bars exceeding 1.0 × (rolling σ × √8); the converging body is the next 12 bars whose
recent half-range is < 0.85 × its earlier half-range (a contracting symmetrical triangle) with a
small net move; the breakout fires when the close escapes the body range **in the pole
direction**, entered at the **next close** (one documented lag). We trade long if the pole was up,
short if down, and measure the forward 5/10/20/60-day **pole-direction** return. Offline &
deterministic once cached; run `python examples/verify.py` to reproduce every number.*

## Data stamp

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Real tape | yfinance daily adjusted (**total-return**) closes for **SPY, QQQ, IWM, DIA, GLD** (public, no key) |
| Window | 2005-01-03 → 2026-05-29 (**As-of 2026-05-31**, partial June dropped; **21.4** years) |
| SPY fingerprint | `4cb5244f3990` (sha1[:12] of the close column, As-of slice) |
| Entries | **109** mechanical pennant breakouts pooled across the 5 tapes (pole_k = 1.0, converge = 0.85) |
| Timing / costs | pole + converging body read on bars **≤ t**; breakout on close of *t*; enter the **next close** (one lag); hold 5/10/20/60 days; **1 bp** one-way × 2 legs per trade |

> **Price-only, no volume.** A textbook pennant also requires *drying-up volume* during the
> consolidation. Daily total-return ETF tapes have no clean, comparable volume, so we test the
> **price geometry only** (pole + contraction + breakout) and state that limitation. The
> mechanical version is the charitable upper bound on the price-shape claim.

## The signal — pennant breakout (pole-direction) vs a drift-matched random baseline

One-sample *t* is the **misleading** number (a long-biased rule on an up-drifting tape inherits
the drift); the **Welch pennant-vs-random** *t* is the test that matters. The random baseline
draws the same number of trades with the **same long/short mix**. Δ = pennant − random.

| horizon | n | pennant | win% | one-sample *t* | random | Δ (penn−random) | net of cost | Welch *t* | *p* |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| 5-day  | 109 | −10.7 bps | 54% | −0.55 | +18.9 bps | **−29.6 bps** | −12.7 bps | −0.87 | 0.387 |
| 10-day | 109 | +13.4 bps | 50% | +0.42 | −14.6 bps | **+28.1 bps** | +11.4 bps | +0.57 | 0.571 |
| 20-day | 108 | +79.4 bps | 61% | +1.96 | +31.3 bps | **+48.1 bps** | +77.4 bps | +0.79 | 0.433 |
| 60-day | 108 | +150.2 bps | 69% | +2.10 | +216.3 bps | **−66.1 bps** | +148.2 bps | −0.58 | 0.564 |

Read it carefully. The one-sample *t* against zero only flirts with significance at the longest
horizons (**+1.96** at 20d, **+2.10** at 60d) — and that is **beta**: the pole-direction trade is
net long ~80% of the time on an up-drifting tape. Against the **drift-matched random baseline**
(matched long/short mix), the deltas are a sign-flipping mess (−29.6 / +28.1 / +48.1 / −66.1 bps)
and the pennant-minus-random Welch *t* **never clears the desk's *t* ≥ 2 bar** (max +0.79 at 20
days, *p* = 0.433). The breakout does not forecast continuation.

## Per-ticker (H = 20) — no coherent cross-sectional edge

| ticker | entries (long) | pennant | one-sample *t* | random | Δ (penn−random) |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| SPY | 26 (24) | +29.4 bps | +0.37 | +42.1 bps | **−12.7 bps** |
| QQQ | 19 (17) | +245.7 bps | +3.36 | −17.3 bps | **+263.0 bps** |
| IWM | 18 (14) | +81.8 bps | +0.77 | −46.9 bps | **+128.7 bps** |
| DIA | 16 (11) | −37.7 bps | −0.43 | +63.6 bps | **−101.4 bps** |
| GLD | 30 (22) | +76.9 bps | +0.96 | +82.4 bps | **−5.6 bps** |

One name (QQQ) carries a single eye-catching delta (+263 bps on **19** trades — a thin,
high-variance count); the other four are flat-to-negative versus random. Positive in 2 of 5,
no sign of a stable, cross-sectional continuation edge — the hallmark of a small-sample fluke
sitting on top of drift.

## Direction-scramble placebo — the thesis test

The pennant's whole claim is **continuation**: trade *in the pole direction*. The decisive null
keeps the exact same breakout **dates** and the same long/short **count** but reshuffles which
sign is attached to which date — forgetting which way the pole pointed. If trading *in the pole
direction* matters, the real result should sit far in the right tail of the scrambled-direction
distribution.

| test | observed pole-direction 20d return | placebo *p* | draws |
|---|--:|--:|--:|
| SPY direction-scramble | +29.4 bps | **0.910** | 500 |

**91% of direction-scrambled draws match or beat the real (pole-direction) result** (*p* =
0.910). The real pole-direction trade sits *below* the middle of the scrambled cloud — so trading
"with the thrust" carries no information. The continuation claim is busted.

## Synthetic positive control — the harness CAN bank a real continuation

On a deterministic tape with a *planted* pennant (a steep pole, a converging pause, then a real
continuation in the pole direction, knob `edge`), the same breakout rule behaves exactly as it
must — so the flat real-tape result is a genuine "nothing there", not a dead detector.

| planted edge | n | pennant | win% | one-sample *t* |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| **0.00** (pure random walk) | 11 | +177.0 bps | 73% | +1.33 |
| **0.60** (real planted continuation) | 59 | +1325.2 bps | 90% | **+10.30** |

With no planted continuation the control sits at *t* ≈ 1.3 (no false positive — averaged over 12
seeds the edge=0 mean *t* is ~0.26, with ~8% exceeding |t| = 2, close to nominal); a real planted
continuation lights up at *t* = +10.30 with a 90% win-rate and ~50 detections matching the ~50
planted events. The detector is live.

## Verdict

- **Signal — NONE.** The pole-direction breakout does **not** beat a drift-matched random
  baseline with a matched long/short mix (Δ = −29.6 / +28.1 / +48.1 / −66.1 bps at 5/10/20/60
  days; the pennant-vs-random Welch *t* never clears 2, max +0.79 at 20 days, *p* = 0.433). The
  only one-sample *t*'s that approach significance (20-day +1.96, 60-day +2.10) are beta — the
  pole-direction trade is net long ~80% of the time on an up-drifting tape.
- **Tradability — MIRAGE.** There is no residual edge once the drift you were always getting is
  removed, and costs only deepen the hole. With ~5 breakouts per instrument per decade there is
  nothing to scale even if there were an edge.
- **"Does the pennant forecast continuation?" — BUSTED.** The direction-scramble placebo leaves
  the result intact (*p* = 0.910): forgetting which way the pole pointed does as well or better
  than trading with it, so the "continuation" is not load-bearing. The pennant is a descriptive
  after-the-fact label, not a forecasting strategy.
